subject.title: Feature: Handle Signal message edits (editMessage envelope)

question: For a Signal message edit, should OpenClaw replace/supersede the original transcript input and suppress a second reply, or retain both inputs and only annotate the correction?
rationale: The edit-target identifier can be parsed mechanically, but transcript mutation, dedupe, mention-gated dispatch, and interaction with a run already in progress are persistent product semantics that a channel-local marker alone cannot safely choose.

options.title: Define structured supersession
options.body: Adopt Signal edit metadata keyed by the target timestamp, suppress non-mentioned edit dispatches, and specify a session-level replacement or supersession rule before implementation.

options.title: Keep an append-only correction trail
options.body: Preserve the original input and append an explicitly marked correction without transcript replacement, accepting that downstream context sees both events.

options.title: Defer mutation semantics to cancellation work
options.body: Limit this issue to typed Signal edit detection and defer transcript replacement or active-run cancellation until the broader cross-channel design in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/55691 is decided.

recommendation.title: Define structured supersession
recommendation.body: Adopt Signal edit metadata keyed by the target timestamp, suppress non-mentioned edit dispatches, and specify a session-level replacement or supersession rule before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The historical Signal monitor and dispatch ownership evidence is strongest for this person, and the decision spans the same inbound pathway.
